stem: The organisation that designates World Heritage Sites is __________.
solution: UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) designates World Heritage Sites.

stem: UNESCO World Heritage Sites are of three types: cultural, natural and __________.
solution: World Heritage Sites are classified as cultural, natural or mixed.

stem: The first Indian sites inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites (in 1983) included the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta Caves and __________.
solution: In 1983 India's first inscriptions were the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta Caves and Ellora Caves.

stem: The only 'mixed' (both cultural and natural) UNESCO World Heritage Site in India is __________.
solution: Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim is India's only mixed World Heritage Site.

stem: Which of the following is a NATURAL World Heritage Site in India?
solution: Kaziranga National Park (Assam) is a natural World Heritage Site.

stem: The bird sanctuary that is a UNESCO natural World Heritage Site in Rajasthan is __________.
solution: Keoladeo National Park (Bharatpur) in Rajasthan is a natural World Heritage Site.

stem: The Sundarbans National Park, a World Heritage Site, is famous for the __________.
solution: The Sundarbans is famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger and its mangrove forests.

stem: The World Heritage Site 'Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Park' is in __________.
solution: The Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Park is in Uttarakhand.

stem: The 'Western Ghats' were inscribed as a World Heritage Site for their __________.
solution: The Western Ghats are a natural World Heritage Site recognised for their exceptional biodiversity.

stem: The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram, a World Heritage Site, was built by the __________.
solution: The Mahabalipuram monuments were built by the Pallavas.

stem: The World Heritage Site 'Group of Monuments at Hampi' was the capital of the __________ empire.
solution: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire.

stem: The Khajuraho Group of Monuments was built by the __________ dynasty.
solution: The Khajuraho temples were built by the Chandela rulers.

stem: The Sun Temple at __________ is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Odisha.
solution: The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha is a World Heritage Site.

stem: The Mahabodhi Temple Complex, a World Heritage Site marking the Buddha's enlightenment, is at __________.
solution: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya marks the site of the Buddha's enlightenment.

stem: The 'Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi' World Heritage Site is located in __________.
solution: The Buddhist monuments at Sanchi are in Madhya Pradesh.

stem: The railway station 'Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus', a World Heritage Site, is in __________.
solution: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (formerly Victoria Terminus) is in Mumbai.

stem: The 'Mountain Railways of India' World Heritage Site includes the Darjeeling, Nilgiri and __________ railways.
solution: The Mountain Railways site includes Darjeeling, Nilgiri and Kalka-Shimla railways.

stem: The stepwell 'Rani ki Vav', a World Heritage Site, is located at Patan in __________.
solution: Rani ki Vav is a stepwell at Patan in Gujarat.

stem: The archaeological site of Nalanda Mahavihara, a World Heritage Site, is in __________.
solution: The ancient Nalanda university (Mahavihara) is in Bihar.

stem: The first Indian city to be declared a UNESCO World Heritage City was __________.
solution: Ahmedabad (in 2017) was the first Indian city inscribed as a World Heritage City.

stem: The 'Pink City' inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2019 is __________.
solution: Jaipur city was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2019.

stem: The Harappan city inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2021 is __________.
solution: Dholavira, a Harappan city in Gujarat, was inscribed in 2021.

stem: The Ramappa (Kakatiya Rudreshwara) Temple, inscribed in 2021, is in __________.
solution: The Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple in Telangana was inscribed in 2021.

stem: The 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas', inscribed in 2023, are in the state of __________.
solution: The Hoysala temple ensembles (Belur, Halebidu, Somnathpur) in Karnataka were inscribed in 2023.

stem: Santiniketan, associated with Rabindranath Tagore and inscribed in 2023, is in __________.
solution: Santiniketan in West Bengal, founded by Tagore, was inscribed in 2023.

stem: The Elephanta Caves World Heritage Site, dedicated to Shiva, are located near __________.
solution: The Elephanta Caves are on an island near Mumbai.

stem: The 'Great Living Chola Temples' World Heritage Site is in __________.
solution: The Great Living Chola Temples (Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Darasuram) are in Tamil Nadu.

stem: The 'Hill Forts of Rajasthan' World Heritage Site includes forts such as Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh and __________.
solution: The Hill Forts of Rajasthan include Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer and Gagron.

stem: The Jantar Mantar, an astronomical observatory that is a World Heritage Site, is in __________.
solution: The Jantar Mantar of Jaipur is a World Heritage Site.

stem: The list of intangible cultural traditions maintained by UNESCO is called the __________.
solution: UNESCO maintains the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

stem: The first Indian tradition recognised in UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage was __________.
solution: Koodiyattam (Sanskrit theatre of Kerala) was among the first Indian ICH elements recognised.

stem: The 'Tradition of Vedic Chanting' is on the UNESCO list of __________.
solution: The Tradition of Vedic Chanting is inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

stem: Which of the following is on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list of India?
solution: Yoga is inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list (2016).

stem: The great religious gathering inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2017 is the __________.
solution: The Kumbh Mela was inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2017.

stem: The festival inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2021 is __________.
solution: Durga Puja in Kolkata was inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2021.

stem: The dance festival inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023 is __________.
solution: Garba of Gujarat was inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2023.

stem: The ritual theatre 'Mudiyettu' and the dance 'Chhau' are both on UNESCO's __________ list.
solution: Both Mudiyettu and Chhau are inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

stem: The 'Sankirtana' ritual singing and drumming inscribed as ICH belongs to __________.
solution: Sankirtana, the ritual singing and dancing of Manipur, is UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

stem: The 'Buddhist chanting of Ladakh' is on UNESCO's list of __________.
solution: The Buddhist chanting of Ladakh is inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

stem: The traditional brass and copper craft of 'Thatheras' inscribed as ICH is from __________.
solution: The craft of the Thatheras of Jandiala Guru, Punjab, is inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

stem: The snake-charmer dance 'Kalbelia' inscribed as ICH belongs to __________.
solution: Kalbelia of Rajasthan is inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

stem: The number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India (as of 2023) is more than __________.
solution: India has over forty (42) UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2023.

stem: The Kaziranga National Park World Heritage Site is famous for the __________.
solution: Kaziranga is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros.

stem: The Manas Wildlife Sanctuary World Heritage Site is located in __________.
solution: Manas Wildlife Sanctuary is in Assam.

stem: The 'Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park' World Heritage Site is in __________.
solution: The Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park is in Gujarat.

stem: The 'Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles' World Heritage Site is in __________.
solution: The Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai were inscribed in 2018.

stem: The Group of Monuments at Pattadakal, a World Heritage Site, was built by the __________.
solution: The Pattadakal monuments in Karnataka were built by the Chalukyas.

stem: The three earliest Mughal monuments among India's World Heritage Sites include the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and __________.
solution: Fatehpur Sikri, along with the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort, is a Mughal World Heritage Site.

stem: The Qutb Minar and Humayun's Tomb, both World Heritage Sites, are located in __________.
solution: The Qutb Minar and Humayun's Tomb are in Delhi.

stem: The Red Fort Complex, a World Heritage Site, was built by __________.
solution: The Red Fort in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.

stem: The 'Great Himalayan National Park', a World Heritage Site, is in __________.
solution: The Great Himalayan National Park is in Himachal Pradesh.

stem: India's World Heritage Sites are jointly protected under the __________ Convention of 1972.
solution: World Heritage Sites are protected under UNESCO's World Heritage Convention of 1972.

stem: The 'Nawroz' (Parsi New Year) inscribed as ICH is a __________ element shared with other countries.
solution: Nawroz is a multinational Intangible Cultural Heritage element shared by several countries including India.

stem: Ellora Caves, a World Heritage Site, are notable for containing monuments of __________ religions.
solution: The Ellora Caves uniquely house Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments.

stem: The concept of a World Heritage Site is that it has __________ value to humanity.
solution: World Heritage Sites are recognised for their outstanding universal value to humanity.

stem: Which of these is an Intangible Cultural Heritage rather than a World Heritage Site?
solution: Ramlila is Intangible Cultural Heritage; the others are World Heritage Sites.

stem: The nodal body in India that nominates sites for UNESCO World Heritage status is the __________.
solution: The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) is the nodal agency for World Heritage nominations.

stem: The 'Ramman' religious festival and theatre, a UNESCO ICH, belongs to __________.
solution: Ramman of Uttarakhand is inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

stem: The Ajanta and Ellora caves are World Heritage Sites located in the state of __________.
solution: Both Ajanta and Ellora caves are in Maharashtra.

stem: India's World Heritage Sites are dominated by __________ sites.
solution: The majority of India's World Heritage Sites are cultural sites.

stem: UNESCO recognition of Indian heritage helps in its __________.
solution: UNESCO recognition supports the conservation and global recognition of heritage.

stem: The Keoladeo National Park is also historically known as the __________ Bird Sanctuary.
solution: Keoladeo National Park is historically known as the Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary.

stem: The traditional yoga tradition was inscribed by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage in the year __________.
solution: Yoga was inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016.
